newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER - JACQUET PUTS EMPHASIS ON ATTACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - JACQUET PUTS EMPHASIS ON ATTACK.

text.p: France coach Aime Jacquet, still looking for the right World Cup attack, included five strikers when he named his squad of 22 on Thursday for next month's Tournoi de France.

Jacquet, whose main preoccupation since a sterile Euro 96 campaign in England last year has been a shortage of goals, picked recent regulars Patrice Loko and Christophe Dugarry for the four-team tournament from June 3-11.
He also included Marc Keller of Karlsruhe, Lyon's Florian Maurice and Nicolas Ouedec who plays for Espanyol, a trio with 10 caps between them.
Maurice has been included after missing most of the season because of an Achilles tendon injury suffered three days after winning his first cap in September.

"We're going to recover lost time and do what we have wanted to do," Jacquet told a news conference as he reflected on frustrated attempts to experiment in attack because of enforced absences to Maurice and Ouedec.
To play in attack just behind the strikers, Jacquet has chosen Internazionale's Youri Djorkaeff, Ibrahim Ba of Bordeaux and Metz winger Robert Pires.
Midfield will be run by Juventus pair Didier Deschamps, the team captain, and Zinedine Zidane, while Arsenal's Patrick Vieira, recently promoted from France's under-21 side, has been retained.
"This is a merger of the base of our Euro 96 team with new elements tried out during the 1996-7 season," Jacquet said.
The squad does not include Euro 96 goalkeeper Bernard Lama of Paris St Germain. He is serving a two-month suspension for using cannabis.
"Lama was at fault vis a vis the law but he's not a cheat or dishonest. He has to assume his sanction as a pro. Time is his best ally," Jacquet said.
Auxerre veteran Lionel Charbonnier has been picked as reserve for Fabien Barthez, a key figure in Monaco's French championship-winning side.

Monaco defender Patrick Blondeau has been dropped after being included in all three of Jacquet's squads for friendlies played since January, while Athletic Bilbao's Bixente Lizarazu is back after an injury-plagued season.
Blondeau's Monaco team mate Martin Djetou, who had a good chance of being included as a central defender or midfielder, was unavailable for selection because of injury.
The tournament, with matches at the World Cup venues of Lyon, Nantes, Montpellier and Paris, includes world champions Brazil, Italy and England.

Defenders - 5-Laurent Blanc (Barcelona), 2-Vincent Candela (AS Roma), 8-Marcel Desailly (AC Milan), 4-Franck Leboeuf (Chelsea), 12-Bixente Lizarazu (Athletic Bilbao), 18-Bruno N'Gotty (Paris St Germain), 15-Lilian Thuram (Parma)
Midfielders - 7-Didier Deschamps, Zinedine Zidane (both Juventus), 19-Christian Karembeu, 3-Pierre Laigle (both Sampdoria), 17-Patrick Vieira (Arsenal), 13-Ibrahim Ba (Bordeaux)

Forwards - 6-Youri Djorkaeff (Internazionale Milan), 9-Christophe Dugarry (AC Milan), 21-Marc Keller (Karlsruhe), 11-Patrice Loko (Paris St Germain), 22-Florian Maurice (Lyon), 20-Nicolas Ouedec (Espanyol), 14-Robert Pires (FC Metz)
